what: Power: JP1 is across J1 (`PWR_SW`), the header for a power switch on a case.
do: Bridge JP1, or wire a switch to J1. Until one is done the backplane has no power.

what: Clock: JP2 is across J4 (`CLOCK_ENBL_SW`), the header for a switch that stops the clock.
do: Bridge JP2, or wire a switch to J4. Until one is done there is no clock on `PHI2`.

what: Clock: JP1 is across J5 (`CLOCK ENBL SW`), the header for a switch that stops the clock.
do: Bridge JP1, or wire a switch to J5. Until one is done there is no clock on `PHI2`.

what: Clock: JP1 is across J3 (`CLOCK ENBL SW`), the header for a switch that stops the clock.
do: Bridge JP1, or wire a switch to J3. Until one is done there is no clock on `PHI2`.

what: Original 6502: grounds pin 1, which is `VSS` on an NMOS 6502 and `VPB` on a 65C02.
do: Leave both open for a 65C02. Bridge JP1, or fit a shunt on J2, only for an original 6502.

what: `EXP`: shunts here join CPU signals (`VPB`, `MLB`, `SOB`, `PHI1O`, `PHI2O`) to the bus's extra pins.
do: Leave it empty unless a project needs one. Never join `EXP0` or `EXP1` in a build that uses cartridges (see *Extra pins*).

what: `EXP`: shunts here join 65816 signals (`VPB`, `MLB`, `MX`, `E`) to the bus's extra pins.
do: Leave it empty unless a project needs one. Never join `EXP0` or `EXP1` in a build that uses cartridges (see *Extra pins*).

what: I/O window: one shunt picks the 1 KB window the board answers in.
do: Fit the shunt beside `$9400`: IO 6, where the BIOS looks for the GPIO Card.

what: Across D1, the diode in the W65C22N's interrupt line.
do: Leave it. The W65C22N's interrupt output is open-drain: it only pulls the line low, so the board works as shipped and D1 isn't needed. To fit a part that drives its interrupt high as well as low, such as a W65C22S, cut JP1 so the interrupt goes through D1.

what: I/O window: one shunt picks the 1 KB window the board answers in.
do: Fit the shunt beside a window no other card uses. The BIOS doesn't look for this board.

what: Across D1, the diode in the W65C22N's interrupt line.
do: Leave it. The W65C22N's interrupt output is open-drain: it only pulls the line low, so the board works as shipped and D1 isn't needed. To fit a part that drives its interrupt high as well as low, such as a W65C22S, cut JP1 so the interrupt goes through D1.

what: `HRDB`: joins the bus's `EXP1` and `EXP0` to the ROM's High ROM disable, so a cartridge can take `$C000–$FFFF`.
do: Fit two shunts on J2, or bridge JP1 and JP2, in a COB that takes cartridges. Leave them open to keep `EXP0` and `EXP1` free (see *Extra pins*).

what: ROM write: joins the ROM's `/WE` to the bus's write strobe, so a program can write the EEPROM in circuit.
do: Leave it open: R2 holds `/WE` high, and the ROM can't be overwritten by mistake. Fit a shunt on J3, or bridge JP3, only to write the ROM in circuit.

what: I/O windows: two shunts pick the two 1 KB windows the banks answer in. Window 1 can be at `$8000`, `$8800`, `$9000` or `$9800`, window 2 at `$8400`, `$8C00`, `$9400` or `$9C00`.
do: Fit one shunt beside `$8000` (IO 1) and one beside `$8400` (IO 2), where the BIOS looks for the RAM Card. One shunt per window, never two and never none. A window's four positions share its select, so a second shunt for the same window ties two of U7's outputs together. R1 and R2 pull the selects low, so a window left without its shunt answers at every address.

what: I/O windows: two shunts pick the two 1 KB windows the banks answer in. Window 1 can be at `$8000`, `$8800`, `$9000` or `$9800`, window 2 at `$8400`, `$8C00`, `$9400` or `$9C00`.
do: Fit one shunt beside `$8000` (IO 1) and one beside `$8400` (IO 2), where the BIOS looks for the RAM Card. One shunt per window, never two and never none. A window's four positions share its select, so a second shunt for the same window ties two of U7's outputs together. The selects have no pull-ups, as on every other card, so a window without its shunt floats and can select the RAM at random.

what: `LATCH EN`: JP1 grounds the bank latch's output enable, which keeps its outputs on; J2 is a header across JP1.
do: Leave it. Cutting JP1 doesn't turn the latch off: it leaves U2's `OE` floating, and J2 can only ground it. Turning the latch off needs JP1 cut and J2 pin 2 wired to VCC, and is only for the untested J4 experiment in the build notes.

what: I/O window: one shunt picks the 1 KB window the board answers in.
do: Fit the shunt beside `$8800`: IO 3, where the BIOS looks for the RTC Card.

what: Interrupt: one shunt sends the board's interrupt to `IRQB` or `NMIB`.
do: Fit the shunt on `IRQB`, which the BIOS expects. With no shunt the interrupt reaches neither.

what: Across D1, the diode in the DS1511Y's interrupt line.
do: Leave it. The DS1511Y's interrupt output is open-drain: it only pulls the line low, so the board works as shipped and D1 isn't needed. To fit a part that drives its interrupt high as well as low, such as a replacement of your own, cut JP1 so the interrupt goes through D1.

what: JP3 feeds `PHI2` to an enable of U3, a 74HC138, so the board is selected only while `PHI2` is high. JP2 would tie that enable high instead.
do: Leave them. With `PHI2` on the decoder's enable, the card's read and write strobes last only while `PHI2` is high, when the 6502's address and data are valid, as the chips need. Tied high, the strobes would run through the whole cycle and glitch while the address settles. Rev 1.1 has no jumpers here: `PHI2` goes straight to the enable.

what: Options for the ACIA's crystal: JP2 adds R1 (1M) across it, and JP3 adds C7 (22pF) to ground.
do: Leave them open for the R6551AP, the part the cards are tested with. Close both for a Rockwell R65C51P1 or R65C51P2, whose oscillator won't start on the bare crystal (an R65C51P2 ran clean this way on 2026-11-11), or for a WDC W65C51.

what: Options for the ACIA's crystal: JP2 adds R1 (1M) across it, and JP3 adds C12 (22pF) to ground.

what: `CTS`: where the ACIA's `CTS` comes from.
do: Fit the shunt on pins 2 and 3, ground, as the boards are built. On pins 1 and 2 it takes `CTS` from the cable, and a cable that doesn't assert it stops the transmitter. With no shunt the input floats, and serial may not work.

what: `DCD`: where the ACIA's `DCD` comes from.
do: Fit the shunt on pins 1 and 2, ground, as the boards are built. On pins 2 and 3 it takes `DCD` from the cable, and a cable that doesn't assert it stops the receiver. With no shunt the input floats, and serial may not work.

what: I/O window: one shunt picks the 1 KB window the board answers in.

what: I/O window: one shunt picks the 1 KB window the board answers in.

what: I/O window: one shunt picks the 1 KB window the board answers in.

what: Interrupt: one shunt sends the board's interrupt to `IRQB` or `NMIB`.
do: Fit the shunt on `IRQB` or `NMIB`, as your program needs. `IRQB` is the usual choice; the BIOS doesn't use this interrupt. With no shunt the interrupt reaches neither.

what: Across D1, the diode in the VERA module's interrupt line.
do: Cut JP2 before fitting a shunt on J5. The VERA module drives its interrupt high as well as low, and only D1 stops it holding `IRQB` high against every other interrupt source. Rev 1.1 ships it open.

what: Across D1, the diode in the VERA module's interrupt line.
do: Leave it open. The VERA module drives its interrupt high as well as low, and D1 lets it only pull `IRQB` low. Bridged, JP2 would let it hold the line high against every other interrupt source. Never bridge it. Fit D1, which the BOM lists: with the jumper open it is the only path to the line, so without it the board never interrupts.

what: Adds R1, a 1k pull-up, to the 5 V side of the interrupt's level shifter (Q1).
do: Leave it open: the CPU board's 10k pull-up on `IRQB` does that job, and two pull-ups would sit in parallel (see *Shared lines*).

what: Across D1, the diode in the interrupt line from Q1, the level shifter the Pico drives.
do: Leave it open. The Pico drives its side of Q1 high as well as low, and Q1's body diode passes that high to `IRQB` whenever another card pulls the line low. D1 lets the card only pull `IRQB` low. Never bridge it. Fit D1, which the BOM lists: with the jumper open it is the only path to the line, so without it the board never interrupts.

what: Video RAM timing: which clock the column latch (U6) takes from U8, a 74HCT04. As shipped it is `/CAS` through three inverters; cut JP4 and JP6 and bridge JP3 and JP5 for one inverter, with less delay.
shipped: JP4 and JP6 bridged, JP3 and JP5 open.
do: Leave them. The tested cards run as shipped.

what: Across D1, the diode in the TMS9918A's interrupt line.
do: Fit D1, which the BOM lists, or bridge JP7 with solder. With JP7 open, D1 is the only path from the TMS9918A's interrupt to J1, so a card without D1 never interrupts. The TMS9918A's interrupt output is open-drain, so either way is right for it: Rev 1.1 ships JP7 bridged. Then fit J1's shunt.

Fit D1, which the BOM lists: with the jumper open it is the only path to the line, so without it the board never interrupts.
